_note: One entry per pavilion route. folder = Plans/<folder>/ (nationality, lower case). slug = design-id stem (<slug>, <slug>-alt, <slug>-reno, <slug>-unk). batch = research order, five routes at a time. Facts are leads to confirm, not readings.

pavilions.name: German Pavilion (Padiglione della Germania)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. Built 1909 as Padiglione Bavarese by Daniele Donghi; German from 1912; remodelled 1938 by Ernst Haiger. Many exhibition-era alterations and survey drawings (1993 Haacke, 2014 Bungalow Germania, 2016 Making Heimat, 2018 Unbuilding Walls, 2023 Open for Maintenance).

pavilions.name: Russian Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1914 by Alexey Shchusev; later renovations.

pavilions.name: French Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1912 by Faust Finzi.

pavilions.name: British Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1887 cafe/tea pavilion (Enrico Trevisanato), converted 1909 by Edwin Alfred Rickards; 2018 'Island' by Caruso St John with Marcus Taylor.

pavilions.name: United States Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1930 by Delano & Aldrich; owned by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation since 1986.

pavilions.name: Dutch Pavilion (Rietveld Pavilion)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1912 pavilion by Gustaf Ferdinand Boberg replaced 1953-54 by Gerrit Rietveld.

pavilions.name: Nordic Pavilion (Norway, Sweden, Finland)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1958-62 by Sverre Fehn.

pavilions.name: Finnish Pavilion (Alvar Aalto Pavilion)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1956 by Alvar Aalto (prefabricated timber); restorations incl. 1976, 1982, 2011.

pavilions.name: Venezuelan Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1954-56 by Carlo Scarpa.

pavilions.name: Austrian Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1934 by Josef Hoffmann with Robert Kramreiter; later extension by Hoffmann.

pavilions.name: Japan Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1956 by Takamasa Yoshizaka; later renovation works.

pavilions.name: Swiss Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1951-52 by Bruno Giacometti.

pavilions.name: Canada Pavilion

pavilions.name: Australian Pavilion

pavilions.name: Korean Pavilion

pavilions.name: Belgian Pavilion

pavilions.name: Hungarian Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1909 by Geza Rintel Maroti; rebuilt 1958 by Agost Benkhard; later restoration.

pavilions.name: Spanish Pavilion

pavilions.name: Czech and Slovak Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1926 by Otakar Novotny; later alterations.

pavilions.name: Danish Pavilion

pavilions.name: Greek Pavilion

pavilions.name: Egyptian Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini (Sant'Elena side). 1932 by Brenno Del Giudice, part of the Padiglione Venezia complex; Egypt from 1952.

pavilions.name: Serbian Pavilion (former Yugoslav Pavilion)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1930s by Brenno Del Giudice (Yugoslavia).

pavilions.name: Polish Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1932 by Brenno Del Giudice.

pavilions.name: Romanian Pavilion
pavilions.facts: Giardini. 1938 by Brenno Del Giudice.

pavilions.name: Venice Pavilion (Padiglione Venezia)

pavilions.name: Central Pavilion (former Padiglione Italia) and Padiglione Italia at the Arsenale (Tese delle Vergini)
pavilions.facts: Giardini Central Pavilion: 1894 Palazzo dell'Esposizione (Enrico Trevisanato), facades 1895/1914/1932, Carlo Scarpa interventions (1948-1968), renovation 2009. Arsenale: Padiglione Italia in the Tese delle Vergini since about 2009-2011.

pavilions.name: Qatar Pavilion (new permanent pavilion)
pavilions.facts: Giardini. Lina Ghotmeh selected 2025; state of design or construction to confirm.

pavilions.name: Giardini and Arsenale site plans, Book Pavilion (James Stirling, 1991) and other non-national structures
pavilions.facts: Site plans of the Giardini and the Arsenale; Stirling and Wilford Book Pavilion (Electa bookshop) 1991; Carlo Scarpa ticket booth 1952.

arsenale_to_scope: Long-lease national spaces in the Arsenale (e.g. Argentina, China, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, Turkey, Peru, Mexico, Ireland, Luxembourg, Chile, Philippines) are halls of historic buildings (Sale d'Armi, Artiglierie, Tese, Magazzini). They are scoped after batch 7; plans of a shared hall go to _site unless they show one country's space.
